best_for: People on Windows or a Mac who merge, split, sign, redact or convert PDFs and want the files to stay on their own computer, plus IT teams deciding whether to roll it out to staff.

points.title: Works without an account, with limits
points.text: On first launch the desktop app offers Stirling Cloud, a company server, or continuing without signing in. That last option is Local Only mode: tools run on your computer and any tool that needs a server is blocked. On managed installs an administrator can require sign-in, which removes Local Only.

points.title: Free plan, then per-user pricing
points.text: At the time of reading, Free costs USD 0 with 57 tools to run by hand and 1,000 automation credits a month, for 1 user on Stirling Cloud or up to 5 on your own server. Team was USD 1 per user per month billed yearly, with 2,500 credits. Enterprise is quoted and adds SAML sign-on, audit logs, SCIM and air-gapped setups.

points.title: Credits apply to automation, not hand edits
points.text: Pipelines, AI, the API and MCP use credits, while tools you run yourself in the editor do not. On your own server one unit covers 25 pages or 5 MB, whichever is larger, and automation stops when credits run out until the next month.

points.title: Open core rather than fully MIT
points.text: The code is MIT except for listed folders, including the proprietary app code, the engine and the desktop editor, which carry their own licences. The project calls itself open-core.

points.title: Windows MSI with managed deployment
points.text: This listing has an x64 MSI that installs machine-wide, for Windows 10 or 11. Stirling documents `msiexec /i ... /qn` with `ALLUSERS=1`, `INSTALLDIR` and properties for the server address, locked connection and update mode. If the window does not appear, install the WebView2 Runtime.

points.title: Arm64 Windows and Linux are not listed here
points.text: Stirling also ships an Arm64 Windows setup.exe, which accepts none of the MSI properties, and Linux packages as .deb, .rpm and AppImage. The Mac build in this listing is a universal DMG for macOS 10.15 or later. Docker and server JAR builds exist for self-hosting too.

points.title: Long Windows history, current Mac only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 68 versions, back to 0.37.1. macOS shows only the current release, 3.5.0.
